one_line: A human-approved WebMCP workspace for evidence-scoped, reversible code changes.
what_it_does: Creates a safe project copy, scopes evidence, proposes exact diffs, requires review, verifies completion, and supports rollback.
leverage_rationale: Structured shared state, evidence locking, exact diffs, approval gates, verification, and rollback make agent coding substantially more reliable than UI driving alone.
leverage_evidence: Frames explicitly show a shared WebMCP workspace and safe copy.
Agent searches context and generates an exact diff without touching originals.
Approval boundary and rollback/proof workflow are visible.
execution_rationale: The frame sheets show a coherent end-to-end review-oriented workflow from safe copy through proposed change and approval, though not a clearly demonstrated applied change.
execution_evidence: Visible project/file context and connected-file views.
Exact diff review screens.
APPROVED review-first boundary and blocked unapproved mutations.
impact_rationale: Addresses real agent-coding failure modes—context waste, unverifiable completion, and irreversible edits—for developers and teams.
impact_evidence: Product centers on deterministic proof and SHA-256 verification.
Human review and instant rollback are explicit goals.
creativity_rationale: The shared evidence workspace and cryptographic proof/rollback framing are a thoughtful, ambitious synthesis for agent-assisted coding.
creativity_evidence: Model-neutral shared workspace concept.
Evidence engine, hash locking, and human-owned commit boundary.
usability_note: Guided safe-copy and review flow appears clear, though the multi-stage process may add overhead.
red_flags: Frames do not clearly show a named tool-call transcript or final applied result.
standouts: Strong safety model with exact diff, approval, verification, and rollback.
advance_reason: Strong leverage and evidence-backed execution for a consequential coding workflow.

one_line: A shadcn-compatible React component system with built-in WebMCP capabilities.
what_it_does: Provides reusable human-and-agent components and migration/doctor CLI tooling for structured interaction with forms, dialogs, tables, and controls.
leverage_rationale: Embedding semantic capabilities at the component layer makes structured agent interaction reusable and materially more reliable than generic DOM automation.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies built-in WebMCP support across reusable components.
Supports structured operations on tabs, inputs, selects, dialogs, checkboxes, and tables.
Frames show a component/system implementation workflow and resulting UI.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a plausible build-to-dashboard workflow and polished resulting interfaces, but explicit WebMCP invocation and end-to-end component behavior are not legible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows project setup, repository/code views, and rendered dashboard.
Visible code/editor and execution-like output.
impact_rationale: A reusable component-level approach could lower the cost of making many existing React apps agent-capable.
impact_evidence: Migration path for existing shadcn projects.
CLI init/add/migrate/doctor workflow described.
creativity_rationale: Treating components as dual-user interfaces—human and agent—is a fresh and ambitious WebMCP abstraction.
creativity_evidence: Component-native rather than page-by-page tool authoring.
Compatibility with both Radix UI and Base UI.
usability_note: Migration and doctor commands suggest a practical developer experience.
red_flags: Video frames imply development workflow but do not clearly expose WebMCP calls.
standouts: Reusable component-level agent contract with migration tooling.
advance_reason: High leverage and impact despite only partial motion evidence of WebMCP execution.

one_line: A human-authority layer that exposes typed CRM tools while gating consequential actions.
what_it_does: Publishes find_customer and create_invoice_draft tools, validates inputs, previews pending work, and keeps commit authority with the human/page.
leverage_rationale: Typed page-owned tools and a commit boundary replace brittle guessing while preserving shared state and human authority.
leverage_evidence: Frames name find_customer and create_invoice_draft.
Page owns contract and validations.
Consequential call remains pending rather than creating an invoice.
execution_rationale: The video clearly communicates a coherent lookup-to-pending-draft flow with validation and lifecycle behavior, though the final commit is intentionally not performed.
execution_evidence: Returned customer CUS-2001 resolves to active customer Araya Niran.
Pending consequential action and invoice count remaining zero.
Tool discovery/pause/resume behavior described.
impact_rationale: Useful for commerce, finance, support, and administrative systems where agent speed must not bypass approval.
impact_evidence: Explicit human control over invoice-like consequential actions.
Validation and recovery are central to the product pattern.
creativity_rationale: The explicit separation between preparation and commitment is a strong interaction-design exploration of agent authority.
creativity_evidence: Agent speed/human authority framing.
Page-owned validation and pending commit boundary.
usability_note: Clear discover/prepare/approve model; extra approval is intentional friction for consequential actions.
red_flags: Demo uses fictional CRM data and does not demonstrate a real external integration.
standouts: Strong visual proof of lookup result, validation, pending action, and no unintended commit.
advance_reason: Excellent evidence-backed WebMCP control model with clear practical value.

one_line: A cited theatre research workspace for searching and comparing productions with WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Answers theatre questions, searches source passages, compares productions, and keeps page-level citations in shared human-agent state.
leverage_rationale: Typed retrieval and comparison tools with visible citations improve precision and repeatability over an agent manually browsing scattered theatre sources.
leverage_evidence: Description names ask_theatre, search_theatre_archive, and compare_productions.
Shared workspace shows request, answer, sources, pages, and excerpts.
Frames show knowledge/evidence results and presentation reuse.
execution_rationale: The frame sequence visibly progresses from discovery prompt to populated knowledge/evidence output, though the exact source text and tool trace are small.
execution_evidence: Input-to-knowledge-to-evidence workflow visible.
Evidence, not guesswork messaging and source-like results.
Output shown in a presentation/document context.

impact_evidence: Specific Broadway/West End audience and source-citation workflow.
Page-level supporting passages are core output.
creativity_rationale: A focused, well-pursued synthesis of theatre research, semantic search, comparison, and citations is notably original for the challenge.
creativity_evidence: Domain-specific research workspace rather than generic chat.
Comparison by venue, opening date, or run length.
usability_note: Single shared workspace and citation-oriented output support researcher verification.
red_flags: Specific tool invocation payloads are not legible in the frame sheets.
standouts: Strong evidence-first research UX in a well-defined niche.
advance_reason: Clear audience, credible value, and strong evidence-oriented product workflow.

one_line: A sales dashboard that exposes structured analytics tools to agents.
what_it_does: Provides dashboard views plus six tools for stores, sales, period comparisons, flavor rankings, summaries, and controlled writes.
leverage_rationale: Structured analytical queries avoid brittle filter/picker navigation and let agents obtain exact dashboard state directly; measured time improvement strengthens the claim.
leverage_evidence: Six named WebMCP tools are described.
Claimed 4m38s without tools versus 36s with tools.
Frames show dashboard and agent activity/write indication.
execution_rationale: The dashboard is visibly coherent and the packet describes a complete tool surface, but frame evidence does not clearly show a full query/result exchange.

Agent activity rail includes a write entry with Undo.
Fictional four-store data model is specific.
impact_rationale: Small business owners need answers beyond canned dashboards, and the product targets a concrete analytics bottleneck without requiring an analyst.

Dashboard tools answer store, period, flavor, and summary questions.
creativity_rationale: The concept is a strong, measured application of WebMCP to dashboard analytics with an interesting write/undo audit surface.

usability_note: Familiar dashboard plus agent activity and Undo appears approachable.

standouts: Concrete niche audience and quantified WebMCP delta.
advance_reason: Strong practical leverage and audience fit, with credible dashboard evidence.

one_line: A teacher-owned marking workspace that lets agents recognize rubric ideas without deciding marks.
what_it_does: Exposes answer, rubric, and state tools; maps agent-recognized rubric IDs to teacher-owned points, hold policy, and release decisions.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP enables a precise division of labor: agent performs semantic recognition while page code retains rubric arithmetic, holds, and release authority—hard to reproduce reliably through generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Nine tools and current page state are explicitly described.
Agent reports rubric line IDs, never point values.
Frames show marking controls, agent contract/calls, and changed held counts.
execution_rationale: The described fourteen-answer workflow and visible teacher/agent contract demonstrate a coherent bounded product, though the frames do not expose every end-to-end call.
execution_evidence: Worked example marks thirteen answers while holding five.
Caution setting changes held count to six.
Teacher remains on same screen with contract and calls visible.
impact_rationale: Teachers face repetitive marking work while grading decisions and communication require accountability; this directly addresses that division of labor.
impact_evidence: Specific short-answer marking audience and rubric workflow.
Hold policy and release authority remain teacher-owned.
creativity_rationale: The narrow agent sentence—recognize rubric ideas, never assign points—forms an unusually clear and original human-agent interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Separation of recognition from assessment decision.
Care-level policy changes automation conservatism.
usability_note: Teacher-centered same-screen workflow and explicit holds support trust, though setup may be specialized.
red_flags: Synthetic local dataset; no production LMS integration shown.
standouts: Excellent authority boundary and safety-conscious educational workflow.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage, impact, and creativity with a well-defined responsible automation boundary.

leverage_rationale: Structured constraints plus deterministic solver execution make agent intent operational without trusting the LLM to invent or validate schedules; shared canonical state and auditability are central.

Staleness detection, infeasibility explanations, and audit timeline described.
execution_rationale: The scope is coherent and technically intentional, with scheduling UI, solver, stale-state handling, and audit flow; the frame sheets show a working scheduling product but not every failure state.
execution_evidence: Scheduling screen and interactive Gantt-style product surfaces visible.
Description specifies model edits, solve, stale detection, and audit history.
Solver is deterministic and browser-based.
impact_rationale: Scheduling with machine downtime, dependencies, deadlines, and urgent jobs is a real high-friction problem for operations teams.
impact_evidence: Concrete job-shop constraints and operator workflow.
Natural-language intent paired with validated optimization.
creativity_rationale: Combining agent translation, human trade-offs, deterministic optimization, stale-state detection, and auditability is ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Agent-native optimization workspace concept.
Explicit separation of AI intent from solver truth.
usability_note: Natural-language constraints help, but optimization concepts and Gantt/audit surfaces remain specialized.
red_flags: Frame evidence cannot independently verify solver outputs or infeasibility cases in detail.
standouts: Strong deterministic-verification architecture for agent planning.
advance_reason: Transformative leverage and ambitious, credible solver-centered workflow.

one_line: A collaborative schematic workbench where people and agents edit and simulate the same circuit.
what_it_does: Exposes circuit inspection, validated authoring, highlighting, and SPICE simulation tied to exact project snapshots.
leverage_rationale: Structured circuit graphs, exact terminals, optimistic hashes, and measured simulation avoid the severe imprecision of pixel-driving a CAD editor and preserve shared visual state.
leverage_evidence: Four named tools inspect, author, highlight, and simulate circuits.
Demo description specifies complete graph creation, highlighting, ngspice, and measured outputs.
Results remain visible in the same schematic workbench.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete design-edit-highlight-simulate workflow and frames show the circuit workbench, though the exact circuit/result text is small.
execution_evidence: Visual schematic editor and agent-native workflow are visible.
Demo changes emitter resistor and simulates again.
Simulation measurements are tied to exact circuit snapshot.
impact_rationale: Electronics learners, designers, and engineers benefit from precise co-editing and simulation without forcing agents through dense visual CAD controls.
impact_evidence: Concrete beta-100 bias-stage example.
SPICE measurements and stability/headroom explanation are practical outputs.
creativity_rationale: The dual-native visual/text circuit model, exact graph authoring, highlighting, and simulation is a memorable and technically ambitious use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: One authoritative circuit for human and agent interfaces.

usability_note: Visual schematic plus structured agent actions supports both experts and learners, though circuit concepts remain specialized.

standouts: Exceptional WebMCP fit for precise structured visual-domain state.

one_line: An agent-native motion editor for composing editable short-form video timelines.
what_it_does: Plans scenes, searches/imports media, composes clips/captions/audio/transitions, validates attribution, and gates export through approval.
leverage_rationale: Typed timeline and media tools let agents manipulate structured edits, attribution, validation, and approval more reliably than dragging a visual editor.
leverage_evidence: Frames show a browser motion-studio/timeline workflow.
Description names inspect, search, storyboard, compose, validate, attribution, and export tools.
One-use storyboard token binds composition to approved plan; export is confirmed.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a broad but coherent compose-to-validate-to-export flow, and the video visibly shows the product/editor states; detailed agent calls are not legible.
execution_evidence: Editable 9:16/16:9 timeline with video, images, captions, audio, transitions.
Demo produces a 16-second Vietnam travel Reel with imported assets.
Approval and attribution controls are part of the workflow.
impact_rationale: Creators and marketers need faster short-form editing while retaining editable work, attribution, and control over exports.
impact_evidence: Concrete creator workflow and ordinary editable timeline output.
Licensed media attribution and local MP4 export are addressed.
creativity_rationale: The combination of agent scene planning with a real editable timeline and one-use approval token is ambitious and distinctive.
creativity_evidence: Storyboard token bound to exact plan.
Agent-native motion studio rather than black-box video generation.

red_flags: External stock/audio availability and complete export are described more strongly than directly legible in frames.
standouts: Editable, attributable output with strong approval semantics.
advance_reason: Strong creative workflow, practical audience value, and meaningful structured-state leverage.
